name: Vedanta Aluminium Metal Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest primary aluminium producer (Jharsuguda, BALCO Korba) with integrated bauxite-alumina (Lanjigarh), captive coal mines and power; ~2.6 Mtpa smelting. Demerged from Vedanta Ltd and listed 2026-06-15 (1:1 with Vedanta shareholders; promoter 56.38%, fully encumbered with GLAS Agency). Q2 FY27: aluminium output 649 kt (record, +5%), alumina +37%, revenue ~Rs22,066-22,324 cr (+41%), EBITDA ~Rs10,100-10,190 cr (45% margin, +83%), PAT Rs6,187 cr (2x), net debt/EBITDA 0.7x. Value-added products ~two-thirds of sales. Mcap Rs1.49 lakh cr, P/E 9.9.

revenue_mix.segment: primary aluminium and value-added products (billets, wire rod, foundry alloy, rolled)

exposures.mechanism: Dominant driver. Output 649 kt/quarter (2.6 Mtpa); +10% LME (~US$320/t) x 2.6 Mt = US$830 mn = Rs7,860 cr (at 94.5) less ~15% hedged/lagged = ~Rs6,700 cr = +17% of annualised Q2 EBITDA (~Rs40,400 cr). EV/MCap 1.19 (mcap Rs1,49,123 cr + net debt ~Rs28,000 cr = 0.7x EBITDA); persistence 0.5 => +17 x1.19 x0.5 = +10. Empirical: no VAML history (listed 2026-06-15); VEDL's pre-demerger +7.22 (t=3.2) is consistent in sign/size. Aluminium is -19.6% since 1 June (Q2 EBITDA margin 45% vs ~30% a year ago) - the Q2 print was struck at higher prices.

evidence.note: Q2 EBITDA +83% on record 649 kt output and higher LME
Q2 revenue Rs22,066 cr, EBITDA Rs10,192 cr, PAT Rs6,187 cr
LME aluminium cash ~US$3,000-3,130 in Oct; stocks 236-241 kt

exposures.mechanism: Coal for alumina refining (Lanjigarh), captive power (BALCO/Jharsuguda, related-party) and calcination. Coal+power ~40% of costs (annual costs ~Rs48,800 cr => ~Rs19,500 cr); captive/linkage mines cover ~60% (Jamkhani, Radhikapur West, Kuraloi, Chotia - model knowledge) so ~40% exposed = Rs7,800 cr; +10% = Rs780 cr = -1.9% EBITDA x1.19 x0.5 = -1.2. Coal e-auction premia ~94% and 74 plants at <=7 days stock make the shock live; government emergency order for captive plants (26-28 Sep) adds diversion risk.

Smelting uses ~14 MWh/t => ~36 TWh/yr; mostly captive/group-captive coal plants, ~20% marginal exposure to market or regulated tariffs at ~Rs6/unit = Rs4,400 cr; +15% = Rs660 cr = -1.6% EBITDA x1.19 x0.4 = -0.8. IEX at Rs20 ceiling on 19 Sep and the El Nino summer-2027 risk (event odds 0.4) give a fat left tail (curtailment of potlines).

evidence.note: IEX Rs20/unit ceiling; Q2 prices ~+46% y/y

exposures.mechanism: Revenue LME-USD-linked (~Rs89,000 cr annualised); USD-linked costs (imported coal/alumina/CP coke/caustic, freight) ~25% of costs = Rs12,000 cr. +3% => +Rs2,670 cr revenue - Rs370 cr costs = +Rs2,300 cr = +5.7% EBITDA x1.19 x0.5 = +3.4; trimmed to 3.0 for hedges and USD debt (US$ bond tap). Domestic aluminium prices also price off LME x INR + duty.

evidence.note: Revenue/EBITDA linked to LME; value-added products 2/3 of sales (SMEStreet headline 2026-10-09)

exposures.mechanism: Carbon anodes (calcined petroleum coke, coal-tar pitch), caustic soda and aluminium fluoride are ~20% of cash costs; +10% feedstock => +2% of costs = Rs976 cr = -2.4% EBITDA x1.19 x0.4 = -1.1. Brent ~US$95 and refinery cracks +15% since June lift pet-coke/pitch prices.

evidence.note: Cost lines up with output growth; Middle East conflict context

exposures.mechanism: Net debt ~Rs28,000 cr (0.7x EBITDA, down Rs3,090 cr q/q) and interest Rs911 cr/q; but 56.38% of VAML is encumbered with GLAS for the promoter's dollar financings, so spread widening feeds group-level forced-sale risk. +50 bp on Rs10,000 cr floating = Rs50 cr is trivial; the weight is the pledge channel.

evidence.note: VAML encumbrance (56.38%) tied to US$400m bond tap

exposures.mechanism: P/E 9.9 on trailing; cyclical with dividend yield 2.1%; +25 bp cost of equity => -0.7; no empirical data (listed June 2026).

evidence.note: P/E 9.94, dividend yield 2.09%, mcap Rs1,49,123 cr

exposures.mechanism: Bauxite pricing and royalty: Odisha HC dismissed VAML's plea for OMC bauxite at the historical Rs1,000/t (booked at Rs3,000/t since April 2026 vs market ~Rs3,800/t). CLSA: one-time up to US$290 mn pre-tax / US$195 mn post-tax (1.2% of mcap) and +US$10/t aluminium cost (~0.5%) near-term; OMC reportedly demands Rs5,600 cr by 31 Oct (SAHI; CLSA's historical dues ~Rs2,500 cr pre-interest - unreconciled). Further royalty/auction premia on Sijimali and other blocks are the structural leg: -1.0.

evidence.note: CLSA: ~US$10/t cost rise, one-time hit up to US$290 mn after Odisha HC order
CLSA keeps Outperform, TP Rs540; muted medium-term impact
OMC demand Rs5,600 cr with 31 Oct deadline (unreconciled)

exposures.mechanism: Aluminium demand from EVs, solar frames, grid cables; value-added products (VAP) now two-thirds of sales supports premiums. +1 treated as +1.5% structural Al demand => +1.0 via multiple. Overlaps with price edge - kept small.

evidence.note: SMEStreet headline: two-thirds of metal sold as value-added products

exposures.mechanism: Anti-dumping probes on Chinese flat-rolled and extruded aluminium products would protect VAP premia; broad probe wave Sep-Oct 2026 (chemicals, APIs, steel). Small share of EBITDA: +0.5.
No empirical history (listed 2026-06-15; -20.6% in 3 months vs aluminium -4.9%). Beta to metals/risk assumed ~1.2 like VEDL: -0.8 per +5 VIX points.

company_links.mechanism: Same promoter (Vedanta Resources/Twin Star), identical shareholder base from the 1:1 demerger and shared GLAS encumbrance structure (54.72% VEDL / 56.38% VAML). Weekly regression of VAML on VEDL since listing: beta 0.46, corr 0.58 (20 weeks only); VAML on HINDZINC 0.56 (corr 0.76). Shrunk for the market component: 0.35.

evidence.note: Promoter-level encumbrance and bond financing disclosure
